newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Ogata wants aid only to integrated Bosnian towns.
newsitem.headline: Ogata wants aid only to integrated Bosnian towns.

text.p: Sadako Ogata, the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees, said on Monday her office would give support only to Bosnian municipalities that permit the return of minority ethnic groups.

Addressing the Security Council, Ogata said only 10,000 refugees have been allowed to return to areas in which they are not a majority whereas local leaders in many other regions sought to build "ethnically pure" cities.

"My office has decided to provide support and material assistance to municipalities and regions which accept minority returns and to withhold it in areas where minority returns are refused," she said, according to her prepared statement.

Ogata, who spoke to the press after briefing Security Council members, said that out of the 2.2 million refugees and internally displaced people, about 520,000 had found a home, since the Dayton peace agreement was signed in 1995. Most of them had found permanent asylum in other countries or went to "so-called majority areas" where their ethnic group dominated.

"I am convinced that ethnic relocation and repopulation cannot be part of a solution for a peaceful and multi-ethnic Bosnia, uness it is voluntary," she said. "And it is genuinely voluntary when people can choose to go back to their homes. We will persist to make that choice possible."
But she said that if the leders of the former Yugoslavia continued in peacetime what they pursued in wartime "we may fail and there is a high risk of hostilities resuming."

Ogata mentioned no names but Serbs have persistently excluded other ethnic groups in areas they control and Bosnia Croats, with apparent acquiesence from Zagreb, have used force to divide the city of Mostar along ethnic lines.
